newsitem.title: GERMANY: German army said ailing from spare parts shortage.
newsitem.headline: German army said ailing from spare parts shortage.

text.p: The German army's shortage of spare parts will not be resolved any time soon because of budget cuts and delivery delays, the army's highest commanding officer said on Thursday,
General Helmut Willmann, the army's inspector, told a news conference in Bonn the shortages had had a negative effect on army morale.
"You should see how frustrating it is for soldiers if they have to wait, for example, for two months just to repair damaged vehicles," said Willmann, a three-star general.

The German media have reported that half the army's tanks and one-fifth of its helicopters are broken but cannot be repaired due to lack of money. There are funds to overhaul only half the trucks needing routine repairs.
Willmann said that to maintain training capacity, only 25 percent of the army's tanks -- rather than 50 percent -- would be mothballed.
"An urgent problem facing the army at the present time is the upkeep of materiel," Willmann said.

He said recently introduced steps to improve the army's readiness would help alleviate shortages in the medium term because it would take time before companies supplying the parts could fill the orders.
Willmann also said the army's readiness was not in doubt. He said the Cold War-era goal of being able to mobilise 90 percent of the armed forces for battle within 48 hours was no longer the standard.
"The readiness needed for the current security conditions is defined as exercise-and-training-capable," he said. "This level is secure for a 233,000-strong army despite tight budgets."
